elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: § 8.2 as rendered retains automatic renewal ("Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives sixty days' advance written notice") rather than mutual written agreement, and the conditional automatic-renewal elements are not all satisfied (opt-out is 60 days, not ≤30, and no Vendor reminder obligation exists). To meet this element the drafter would need either a mutual-written-agreement renewal or a 30-day opt-out plus a 60-day Vendor reminder.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: § 8.2: "Each Order Form renews for twelve months" — renewal term is exactly 12 months, within the ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 8.2 requires "sixty days' advance written notice" to stop renewal; 60 > 30. Defect: the notice figure must be reduced to thirty days (or fewer) for Customer's non-renewal notice.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Neither § 8.2 nor § 8.3 contains any Vendor renewal-reminder obligation; § 8.3's ninety-day notice relates only to a price increase, not to the fact of renewal. Defect: no operative sentence requiring Vendor to notify Customer at least 60 days before each renewal.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: § 8.3 (unchanged): "Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent." This is literally the lesser-of-CPI-and-3% formulation.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 8.2: "unless either Party gives sixty days' advance written notice." Sixty days equals the 60-day ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a matching artifact — the figure is spelled out in words ("sixty") rather than digits; in substance the window is 60 days.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: § 8.3 caps uplift at "the lesser of the increase in the ... Consumer Price Index ... and three percent," which is necessarily ≤ 5 percent; already met without edit.

reasons: The single edit replaces "one hundred eighty days" with "sixty days" in § 8.2; nothing else in §§ 8.2–8.3 is touched, no extras (survival tails, procedures, reminder mechanics) are added, and the favourable CPI/3% cap, the ninety-day price-increase notice, and the prepaid-period carve-out are retained. That is the smallest change needed to reach a complete fallback level.
Fallback is complete: the non-renewal window is sixty days (≤60) and the retained § 8.3 uplift cap (lesser of CPI and three percent) is comfortably within the 5 percent ceiling.

Preferred is not complete: the opt-out window remains sixty days rather than thirty, and no Vendor reminder at least sixty days before renewal is imposed anywhere in the operative text; the margin comment correctly notes these as short-of-preferred rather than claiming them.

Intent is preserved: the mutual ("either Party") notice structure, twelve-month renewal term, price-increase notice period, and prepaid-period protection survive without contradiction; no defined term, cross-reference, or commercial mechanic is left dangling.

The deterministic "non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days: number not found" result is a false negative caused by the numeral being written in words; inspected in substance, § 8.2 now reads "sixty days' advance written notice," which satisfies the fallback threshold.
The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: the original one-hundred-eighty-day window exceeded both the 60-day fallback ceiling and the 90-day walk-away threshold.
